answer: One concrete defense is a slashable identity bond: before an agent may trade, it locks capital against a unique key. Think of a jetty where every piling costs real coin, so an attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must post a thousand bonds, and the cost rises linearly with the Sybil count. Peers who catch two identities colluding slash the whole stake, making a fabricated grove of agents a net loss instead of a profit. Honest agents recover their bond on exit, riding out any tide of suspicion with their capital intact.
